messages:
Lina (Support): heads up — ACME reported users getting kicked to login after MFA enrollment and seeing a 401 with "invalid_session" in the app. Started when they enabled the new device-trust flow yesterday evening.

acme_admin: yea, noticed it around 18:10 UTC. Some users (mobile + web) get redirected to SSO, they authenticate, then land back in the app but are immediately logged out. No obvious errors in browser console.

Lina (Support): repro steps from customer: 1) login via SSO (Okta) 2) complete MFA (Authenticator app) 3) opt-in to "Remember this device" 4) app redirects to /dashboard then instant sign-out. Happens ~30-90s after redirect.

Marco (Eng-Auth): pinging in, assigning priority. This smells like session cookie rotation or SameSite flag mismatch when we exchange assertion after MFA. Any chance their cookie domain changed?

acme_admin: they did a CDN config change (new host header) around the same time but said it was reversible. Not sure it should affect cookie domain if host header preserved.

Priya (SRE): also see an uptick of 401s in the last deploy window. Running a quick query — lots of 401s with backend message: "session validation failed: nonce mismatch". Could be stale KV for device-trust tokens.

Lina (Support): attached their logs (redacted):
```
2025-12-04T18:12:03Z INFO auth: assertion received for user x@y.com
2025-12-04T18:12:03Z INFO auth: created session id sess_7b3f
2025-12-04T18:12:05Z WARN auth: validate_session(sess_7b3f) failed: nonce mismatch
2025-12-04T18:12:06Z INFO proxy: set-cookie: rwd_session=...; Domain=acme.example.com; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=None
2025-12-04T18:12:35Z INFO auth: session expired check: token not found in device-kv
```

Marco (Eng-Auth): thanks. Two hypotheses: 1) device-kv lease short/evicted causing newly-created assertion to reference a missing nonce on validation; 2) sticky sessions/proxy rewriting host header and cookie domain mismatch so browser sends old cookie while server expects new session id.

Priya (SRE): I'm seeing the node that handles assertion creation is a different pod than the one doing validation ~20% of the time due to recent LB change. If device-kv was local-only (we had a misconfig in the rollout), that would explain nonce missing on validation. Checking config now.

deploy-bot: deployment 2025.12.04-1437 rolled to region us-east-1 by @Marco, configuration change: upstream-proxy sticky-session=false -> true (canary).

Marco (Eng-Auth): ohhh that explains it. We merged a patch to enable sticky sessions but the KV client config for device-nonce was accidentally left as local memcache in the canary. So when requests hit a different pod, they can't read the nonce.

Lina (Support): so customer sees successful login then the app validates and cannot find nonce -> treats it as invalid session -> sign-out?

Marco (Eng-Auth): yep. Short-term workaround: tell ACME to disable the canary CDN host header change or route their traffic to a single instance (yah, not great). Longer-term fix: switch device-nonce store to central Redis and/or propagate nonces via shared KV and add a fallback validation allowing short re-check window.

acme_admin: any mitigations we can give to users now? They have many non-technical users complaining.

Priya (SRE): we can roll back the canary sticky flag on the upstream proxy in us-east-1; that should reduce cross-pod hits and cut errors. I'll coordinate rollback if Eng ok.

Marco (Eng-Auth): do the rollback. Also I'll push a fix to device-nonce client to use redis (feature flagged off by default) and enable it for ACME tenant after tests.

Lina (Support): telling customer: rollback + clear their session cookies ("Sign out of all devices" flow) may help immediate cases. We'll also ask them to avoid the CDN host header change until we confirm fix.

acme_admin: rolling back upstream-proxy sticky flag now. Status: in progress.

deploy-bot: rollback started for upstream-proxy flag in us-east-1 (id: rb-20251204-01).

Priya (SRE): monitoring 401 rate — dropping already from 18.5% -> 2.3% in last 6 minutes. Nice.

Marco (Eng-Auth): follow-ups: 1) patch device-nonce client to Redis + test; 2) add observability: tag sessions created during MFA with pod id and nonce existence check metric; 3) docs: known issue with canary memcache config. I'll open PRs.

Lina (Support): I'll send ACME a step-by-step: clear cookies, sign out all devices, try login, and we'll update when patch merges. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

acme_admin: confirmed users can log back in after sign-out+rollback. Thanks team.

Marco (Eng-Auth): filing postmortem notes and ETA on fix. ETA for Redis switch: 48h canary, 7d full rollout.

Priya (SRE): adding runbook entry: on sudden MFA session invalidations check (a) KV config for device-nonce, (b) LB/sticky session flags, (c) cookie domain/SameSite after CDN changes.

Lina (Support): closing the support ticket for now, will reopen if ACME sees regressions.

acme_admin: thx all!
